prevention.title: Lunar Habitat Fire Safety Insights

findings.text: Solid-fuel microgravity tests measured oxygen up to 22.2% at 101 kPa, showing ignition and flame spread limits for materials like PMMA and Nomex.
Gas-fuel diffusion flame experiments in microgravity self-extinguished at oxygen levels as low as 13.5%, indicating strong dependence on oxygen concentration for flame stability.
All available microgravity and 1 g combustion data bound possible behavior on the Moon, but no partial-gravity experiments are present in the dataset.

prevention.implication: Design lunar habitat fire-safety systems assuming that gas-fuel fires may self-extinguish below ~14% O2 and solid-fuel fires can sustain up to ~22% O2 at cabin pressure, while planning for higher O2 levels needed for crew life support.
prevention.gap: The data do not include any combustion tests performed in lunar-gravity (0.16 g) or Mars-gravity conditions.

detection.title: Lunar Habitat Fire Detection Gaps

findings.text: Solid-fuel microgravity tests measured smoke at 21% oxygen and 101 kPa, which differs from the planned lunar base environment of ≥30% oxygen and ≤70.3 kPa.
Gas-fuel microgravity experiments also used 21% oxygen at 101 kPa, providing no data for the lower pressure range expected on the Moon.
All cited investigations were conducted in microgravity, indicating that partial-gravity combustion data are not present in the PSI archive.

detection.implication: Designers cannot rely on existing PSI data to predict fire behavior under the reduced pressure and higher oxygen conditions of a lunar base.
detection.gap: The dataset lacks experimental results for partial-gravity, lower-pressure, and ≥30% oxygen environments.

suppression.title: Fire suppression limits for lunar habitats

findings.text: Liquid fuel droplets of methanol and heptane extinguished in microgravity at measured oxygen as low as 12.0% with nitrogen diluent, well below the planned 30% oxygen for a lunar base.
Solid fuels such as PMMA and Nomex showed extinction at measured oxygen concentrations between 13.6% and 22.2% in microgravity at 101 kPa cabin pressure.

All 66 lunar-base condition tests used gas fuels at 30% oxygen or higher and pressures ≤70.3 kPa, indicating that existing data focus on gas-fuel scenarios rather than liquids or solids at those conditions.

suppression.implication: Designers should expect that both liquid and solid fuels can be extinguished at oxygen levels far below the planned 30% and that suppression strategies can rely on diluents effective at those lower concentrations.
suppression.gap: The data do not include partial-gravity combustion results or solid-fuel tests at the specific lunar-base pressure limit of 70.3 kPa.
